clickResults.label: FIRST-RUN SETUP Install CAVRA with a safe default environment before connecting agents. CAVRA now includes a built-in setup path for Community operators: initialize defaults, generate a known demo workspace, configure report delivery by secret reference, list policy-controlled actions, validate runtime decisions, and seed AISPM activity without asking users to invent risky files by hand. Open Setup Guide Review Policies View AISPM SETUP WIZARD Local Community Accept safe defaults or edit policy/report settings. Create demo workspace with known allow/block scenarios. Configure SMTP using a deployment secret reference. Run validation and record decisions for AISPM. Mark setup complete before agent onboarding. CONFIGURED BY `CAVRA SETUP INIT` Default setup state Creates a safe Community baseline with policy pack, evidence location, AISPM enabled state, agent defaults, and report-delivery placeholders. GENERATED BY `CAVRA SETUP DEMO-ENV` Demo workspace Creates known safe and risky files such as `.env`, IAM Terraform, Kubernetes delete examples, and deploy scripts so users can prove decisions immediately. RUN BY `CAVRA SETUP VALIDATE` Validation scenarios Exercises read, write, command, Git, and MCP decisions and can record events into the activity store for AISPM posture views. CONFIGURED BY `CAVRA SETUP SMTP` SMTP report setup Collects host, port, sender, recipient allowlist, and secret reference without storing the SMTP password in setup state. LISTED BY `CAVRA SETUP POLICY-ACTIONS` Policy action catalog Shows block, allow, approval, and trust entries from the active policy pack so operators can plan add, update, and delete changes. EXPOSED THROUGH `/SETUP/*` APIS GUI/API setup flow Self-hosted front ends can call setup status, defaults, bootstrap, SMTP test, demo workspace, validation, complete, and policy catalog endpoints. INTERACTIVE LOCAL WIZARD Run first-run setup from the browser when the local API is connected. This panel uses the same `/setup/*` and `/policy-action-catalog/*` endpoints as the CLI. If no API is reachable, it remains a safe static guide for the public sandbox. Connected to http://localhost:8000. Setup is configured and complete. headingOutline.text: Deterministic controls for risky AI-agent actions.
Start with safe defaults before connecting AI agents.

interactiveElements.label: POLICY ENFORCEMENT Deterministic controls for risky AI-agent actions. Example: an agent attempts to modify an IAM admin role. CAVRA evaluates the actor, target,

clickResults.label: POLICY ENFORCEMENT Deterministic controls for risky AI-agent actions. Example: an agent attempts to modify an IAM admin role. CAVRA evaluates the actor, target, branch, environment, tool trust, and blast radius, then blocks or routes for approval. POLICY Secrets exposure Block reading private keys, `.env`, customer records, or production credentials. Recommended action: Use managed secret references and redacted evidence. POLICY Production mutation Require approval for IAM, deployment, infrastructure, or protected branch changes. Recommended action: Route to platform or security owner with signed attestation. POLICY Untrusted MCP tool Block MCP servers that request filesystem, shell, network, or token capabilities without trust registration. Recommended action: Register server, declare capability, and rerun trust check. POLICY Release bypass Prevent agents from bypassing required checks, tags, release evidence, or protected branches. Recommended action: Attach CAVRA evidence before merge or release. POLICY Context gaps Warn or block when ownership, data classification, change window, or environment tier is missing. Recommended action: Collect missing context before execution. POLICY Report delivery Keep SMTP/provider secrets, recipients, private report contents, and logs outside public Community. Recommended action: Configure a self-hosted report provider or use CAVRA Managed.
